newsitem.title: EGYPT: Egypt senior cleric says will donate organs.
newsitem.headline: Egypt senior cleric says will donate organs.

text.p: One of the Sunni Moslem world's highest religious authorities has said he will donate his organs for transplants when he dies and called on others to do the same, the government newspaper al-Akhbar said on Thursday.
It said Sheikh Mohammed Sayyed Tantawi made the comments to the ruling National Democratic Party's medical committee but it was not clear when.

"The eminent Grand Sheikh of al-Azhar Sayyed Tantawi announced he would donate all his healthy organs after his death to the sick and called on all members of the medical committee to do the same so that they would be role models and pioneers in the line of donors," al-Akhbar said.

Moslem clerics disagree on whether Islamic law allows such procedures. Clerics who oppose transplants base their argument on what they say is uncertainty in the medical profession on the exact time of death.

Tantawi is considered a liberal among Egyptian Moslem clerics. He has condemned female circumcision, which is widespread in Egypt but is described by some opponents of the procedure as genital mutilation. He has also said Islam does not ban interest on bank accounts.
